newsitem.title: CHILE: Soquimich sees $200 mln cement investment.
newsitem.headline: Soquimich sees $200 mln cement investment.

text.p: Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile SA (Soquimich) plans a $200 million investment in the next two and a half years to build cement processing plants in northern Chile with a total capacity of 1.5 million tonnes a year.
The company said in a statement it will exploit high-grade limestone reserves in Chile's Third Region "with the purpose of producing and distributing cement in Chile."
It would be the first incursion into the cement business for Soquimich, the world's largest maker of iodine and a major producer of nitrates and lithium in Chile's arid northern reaches.

It said it based its entrance into the cement industry in Chile on the positive growth prospects of the business and several competitive advantages, including extensive natural resource holdings that will allow low production costs, experience in big products over the past three years, and an existing distribution network comprised of more than 70 distributors and 180 warehouses in Chile.
Cement consumption in Chile has been growing by an average 11 percent a year over the past five years, reaching 3.7 million tonnes in 1996, it said.
